package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly designed to deliver and execute Discord information-stealing malware. It contains postinstall scripts that launch bundled Windows executables (lib.exe and lib2.exe), which exfiltrate sensitive user data, steal Discord tokens, payment information, and deploy further malware. The entire package is a vehicle for malware delivery and has no legitimate functionality.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code executes two bundled Windows executables (lib.exe and lib2.exe) using Node.js child_process, resulting in the launch of malware payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Invoking native executables during npm package installation is highly unusual and a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not execute bundled Windows binaries on install; legitimate postinstall scripts are typically used for build steps or dependency management.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may use postinstall scripts for native module compilation, but not for launching arbitrary executables.
key_indicators: Execution of bundled .exe files via postinstall
No legitimate build or install purpose

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after postinstall, when lib.exe is executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads Discord and browser data, extracts tokens and payment information, and exfiltrates this data to a hardcoded Discord webhook via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating user credentials, tokens, and payment data is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not harvest and transmit sensitive user data to external webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security auditing tools may access similar data, but only with explicit user consent and never exfiltrate to third-party webhooks.
key_indicators: Harvesting of Discord tokens and browser data
Collection of payment and billing information

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after postinstall, when lib2.exe is executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code connects to a hardcoded Discord webhook, downloads a malicious ZIP archive, extracts it, and executes additional malware binaries (osloader.exe and winresume.exe).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing further payloads from remote sources is a classic dropper behavior, enabling multi-stage attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not download and execute arbitrary binaries from Discord webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download updates, but from trusted, authenticated sources—not Discord webhooks.
key_indicators: Download of ZIP from Discord webhook

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after osloader.exe and winresume.exe are executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attempts privilege escalation, installs a backdoor, captures keystrokes and screenshots, accesses the webcam, and opens a REST API on port 20202 for command-and-control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: These are advanced, multi-capability malware behaviors designed for persistence, surveillance, and remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not perform privilege escalation, keylogging, or open C2 APIs without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may have similar features, but require explicit user consent and are not delivered via npm packages.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// C# pseudocode (reverse engineered):
If running in VM or analysis environment, delay execution for several minutes before performing malicious actions;
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code detects virtualized or analysis environments and delays execution to evade automated analysis and sandboxes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Delaying execution to evade detection is a common anti-analysis technique in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not intentionally delay or alter behavior based on environment analysis.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some software may check for VMs for licensing, but not to evade detection.

attack_chain.action: During npm package installation, postinstall script executes bundled Windows malware (lib.exe and lib2.exe).
lib.exe harvests Discord tokens, browser data, and payment information, then exfiltrates to attacker's Discord webhook.
lib2.exe acts as a dropper, downloading a ZIP archive from a Discord webhook, extracting it, and launching further malware (osloader.exe, winresume.exe).
osloader.exe and winresume.exe perform advanced malicious actions: privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot capture, webcam access, and establish a C2 REST API on port 20202.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise and remote control

attack_chain.action: lib.exe delays execution in VM or analysis environments to evade detection.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall scripts executing bundled .exe files
Harvesting and exfiltration of Discord tokens and browser data
Network connections to Discord webhooks for data exfiltration or payload download
Dropper behavior: downloading and executing additional binaries from remote sources
Establishing local REST API servers (e.g., on port 20202) for C2
Privilege escalation, keylogging, screenshot, and webcam access
Delayed execution or environment checks to evade analysis
file_indicators: Presence of lib.exe, lib2.exe in npm package tarball
network_indicators: Connections to Discord webhooks for payload download (e.g., https://discord.com/api/webhooks/770716126988599316/o7GXYebuPQzx7RQFUD4cTOPMq2gGicypOMyNpFVQsIb9qyVW2bgZ4MMT6c7jvGEDO5Y6)
Outbound traffic to Discord domains from npm install context
Local REST API server on port 20202
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that execute .exe files, especially lib.exe and lib2.exe. Flag any network connections to Discord webhooks during or after installation. Detect the presence of suspicious binaries (lib.exe, lib2.exe, osloader.exe, winresume.exe) in node_modules or temporary directories. Watch for processes that open local REST APIs on uncommon ports (e.g., 20202) or exhibit keylogging, screenshot, or webcam access behaviors. Use endpoint security tools to alert on privilege escalation attempts and anti-analysis timing delays.
